case_title: RAJ SINGH v. STATE OF HARYANA ETC.
aggravating_circumstances: Appellant was the aggressor, fired at close range, caused death unnecessarily
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 304 Part I IPC, acquitted others
high_court_outcome: Converted conviction to Section 302 IPC, maintained life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused, Raj Singh, and his brothers were involved in a confrontation with the complainant, Bharat Singh, and his brothers. The incident occurred at the house of the complainant. The accused were armed with weapons, including a licensed pistol and country-made pistols. During the altercation, the accused fired shots, resulting in the death of the complainant's brother, Girdhari. The prosecution argued that the accused acted in self-defense, but the court found that the accused were the aggressors and that their actions were not justified as self-defense. The trial court convicted Raj Singh under Section 304 Part I IPC, but the High Court converted the conviction to Section 302 IPC and maintained the life imprisonment sentence.
